::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Novr 11th [1863]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 7-8
:::

[Sir](people/person_939.qmd), 
I have now heard from Messrs [Longman](organizations/other_153.qmd), so that I can proceed in the matter on which I wrote to you some weeks since.

I should be obliged if you would let me know whether you would undertake my works hitherto in [Messrs Parker](organizations/other_152.qmd)’s hands, namely

[The Heir of Redclyffe](cmy_books/cmybook_15.qmd)

[Heartsease](cmy_books/cmybook_19.qmd)

[Daisy Chain](cmy_books/cmybook_24.qmd)

[Dynevor Terrace](cmy_books/cmybook_27.qmd)

[Hopes and Fears](cmy_books/cmybook_37.qmd)

[Little Duke](cmy_books/cmybook_20.qmd)

[Lances of Lynwood](cmy_books/cmybook_23.qmd)

[Marie Theresè of Lamourous](cmy_books/cmybook_31.qmd)

[The Young Stepmother](cmy_books/cmybook_38.qmd)

the stock and stereotypes being transferred to you. All these have been hitherto on commission, and would I suppose so continue until the present [copies on hand](organizations/other_155.qmd) are sold off. I find there are 900 of the Heir of Redclyffe and 700 of Heartsease - and I suppose you would hardly recommend venturing on a cheaper edition till these are disposed of.

Of the Daisy Chain there are 312 on hand, and perhaps this might be the best to put into a cheap form first, as it does not belong quite to the same series as the other, there has always been a fair demand for it, and railway stall keepers say they should sell it in large numbers if it were cheaper. 

Should you be willing to bring out such an edition and at what rate would you allow me per 1000?

I remain
Yours faithfully
C.M. Yonge

---

**Note:** Black-edged paper.
